candidates.description: Noise in the second half of a spoken passage impairs retention of information presented in the first half of the passage
candidates.citation_sentence: Thus, in the current investigation, we attempt to replicate the finding that noise in the second half of a passage can impair retention of material presented in the first half of the passage (Rabbitt, 1968).
candidates.notes: Experiment 1a (SNR = -1) found a significant effect in the opposite direction (noise slightly improved first-half recall, B = 0.26, p = 0.04), but authors hedge with 'some evidence for the opposite claim'; coded inconclusive per codebook hedging criterion [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.description: Rabbitt's Experiment 3 claimed that presenting noise during the second half of a spoken passage impairs retention of information presented in the first half.
candidates.citation_sentence: Thus, in the current investigation, we attempt to replicate the finding that noise in the second half of a passage can impair retention of material presented in the first half of the passage (Rabbitt, 1968).
